content.value_statement: Airflow DAGs can fail when dependencies, retries, and sensors are designed poorly. This skill gives practical patterns for reliable pipeline orchestration.
actual_capabilities: Explains core DAG design principles for idempotent and observable workflows.
Shows dependency patterns for linear flows, fan-out, fan-in, and joins.
Provides TaskFlow API examples for extract, transform, load, and notifications.
Demonstrates dynamic DAG generation for similar pipelines.
Covers sensors for files, S3 objects, external DAGs, and API readiness.
Outlines testing patterns for DAG loading, dependencies, cycles, and task logic.
limitations: It does not run or validate Airflow DAGs in your environment.
Examples use placeholder sources and must be adapted before production use.
It does not cover every Airflow provider or executor configuration.
Security, secrets, and access controls need separate environment-specific review.

use_cases.title: Create a New ETL DAG
use_cases.description: Design a daily extract, transform, and load workflow with clear task dependencies and retries.

use_cases.title: Standardize DAG Patterns
use_cases.description: Define shared conventions for sensors, callbacks, and project structure across many Airflow pipelines.

use_cases.title: Improve Pipeline Tests
use_cases.description: Add focused tests that confirm DAG loading, expected dependencies, and reusable task behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic DAG
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a scheduled workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Airflow DAG for a daily batch job. Include start and end tasks, retries, and clear dependency order.

prompt_templates.title: Use TaskFlow for ETL
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for cleaner Python task structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TaskFlow API ETL pipeline with extract, transform, load, and notify tasks. Explain how data passes between tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Sensors and Branching
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with external readiness checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an Airflow DAG that waits for an upstream data file, checks quality metrics, and branches based on the result.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Airflow DAG design for retries, timeouts, catchup behavior, observability, testing, and deployment structure.

output_examples.input: A team needs a daily customer ETL workflow.
output: A DAG outline with start, extract, transform, load, notify, and end tasks.
Recommended retry, catchup, schedule, and max active run settings.
Notes about idempotent task behavior and logging expectations.

output_examples.input: A pipeline must wait for an S3 file and an upstream DAG.
output: A sensor strategy that uses reschedule mode to protect worker capacity.
A dependency plan that joins readiness checks before processing starts.
Timeout and poke interval guidance for production operations.

output_examples.input: A repository needs basic DAG tests.
output: A test plan for DAG import errors, task counts, schedules, and dependencies.
Suggestions for isolating task business logic from Airflow runtime setup.

best_practices: Keep DAG files lightweight and move heavy business logic into importable modules.
Use reschedule mode for long-waiting sensors to preserve worker capacity.
Test DAG loading, dependency shape, and task logic before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not put expensive processing directly in DAG parse time.
Do not rely on mutable global state inside task logic.
Do not enable catchup or depends-on-past behavior without a clear operational reason.

faq.question: Does this skill write production DAGs automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples. You must adapt and test the DAGs in your Airflow environment.

faq.question: Which Airflow features does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It focuses on DAG structure, TaskFlow API, operators, sensors, branching, callbacks, and tests.

faq.question: Can it help with dynamic DAG generation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a factory pattern for creating similar DAGs from configuration.

faq.question: Does it cover cloud provider setup?
faq.answer: Only at the pattern level. Provider credentials, connections, and infrastructure need separate configuration.

faq.question: Is it suitable for new Airflow users?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts with basic dependency patterns before moving into sensors, branching, and testing.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to test DAG loading, task dependencies, cycles, and individual task logic.
